initial_requirements: The Southwest Florida Water Management District needs a GIS-based Water Use Tracking System for District employees and external customers. The system should support spatial and temporal analysis of regulatory and resource-management data, particularly permitted and actual water use. It is intended to replace inconsistent manual and semi-automated analyses and help staff evaluate water-use trends and assess the effects of management rules.

messages.content:
Hello, I’m GPTREI, your requirements elicitation assistant. I’ll be gathering detailed information about the Water Use Tracking System so we can clearly understand what it needs to do and who it needs to support.

Before we begin, are your expectations for this interview aligned with that scope, or would you like to add or adjust anything?

Yes, that scope sounds right. We’re mainly looking for a GIS-based system that helps our staff and external users track permitted and actual water use, analyze trends over time, and better understand the effects of management rules. If anything needs to be adjusted, it would mostly be around making sure the system fits our current regulatory workflows and data sources.
To start off, could you please introduce yourself and your connection to this project?

I’m speaking as someone involved with the District’s water use and resource management work, so I’m familiar with how the current analyses are done and where the pain points are. My perspective is mainly from the staff side, where we need better tools for reviewing permits, comparing reported use, and doing spatial and temporal analysis more consistently.
Thank you. Can you describe the current process or system you use for reviewing permits, comparing reported water use, and performing spatial or temporal analysis?

Right now it’s a mix of GIS tools, spreadsheets, database queries, and a lot of manual compilation. Different staff members often build their own workflows to compare permitted versus actual use, so the results can vary a bit depending on who is doing the analysis. For spatial and time-based review, we usually pull data from several sources and then stitch it together outside of one central system.
What current processes do you want to change or improve, or what features are you hoping to get from this project?

We want to reduce the manual steps and make the analysis more consistent across staff. It would help a lot to have a single place where users can view permits, actual use, and GIS layers together, then run common comparisons without rebuilding the same reports every time. We also want better trend analysis over time so staff can assess whether management rules are having the intended effect.

So the main features/functions you want are: a single place to view permits, actual use, and GIS layers together; common comparison and reporting tools without rebuilding reports; trend analysis over time; and support for assessing the effects of management rules. Is that correct?
Yes, that’s correct. That captures the main goals pretty well, especially the need for a more consistent and centralized way to work with the data.
Are there any other features you would like to see in this project, perhaps something that has not been the primary focus so far?

It would be useful to have good search and filtering so staff can quickly find a permit, user, or geographic area. I’d also expect exports or printable outputs for sharing results, and some level of role-based access since not every external customer should see the same information as internal staff.
Based on your description, do you think integration with existing District data sources and GIS layers should also be included as a core feature?

Yes, definitely. Integration is really important because the system won’t be useful if staff still have to manually pull data from separate District systems and layer it together themselves. We’d want it to connect cleanly to the existing water use, permit, and GIS data sources as part of the core functionality.
Could you prioritize the features we’ve identified so far from most important to least important?

The top priority is integrating the existing District data sources and GIS layers, because that’s what makes the whole system usable. Right after that, I’d put the single workspace for viewing permits, actual use, and maps together, since that’s the main daily workflow. Then I’d rank the comparison and reporting tools, followed by trend analysis over time and the ability to assess management rules, with search, filtering, and export features close behind as supporting capabilities.
Please elaborate on what you want the integrated data sources and GIS layers feature to accomplish.

It should pull together the key permit, reported use, and spatial data so staff can see a complete picture without jumping between systems. Ideally the GIS layers would line up with the water use records by permit, user, location, and time period so people can map and analyze what is happening in a specific area or for a specific permit. If possible, it should also reduce duplicate data entry and keep the information current enough for day-to-day regulatory work.
